ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle BAC=130^\circ$, $AB=AC$, and the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ intersects $BC$ at point $D$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC,\\
it follows that AD=CD,\\
thus, $\angle C=\angle CAD$,\\
since AB=AC,\\
it also follows that $\angle B=\angle C$,\\
in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC+\angle B+\angle C=180^\circ$,\\
therefore, $130^\circ+2\angle C=180^\circ$,\\
solving this, we find $\angle C=25^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle ADB=\angle CAD+\angle C=25^\circ+25^\circ=50^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle BAD=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle ADB=\boxed{105^\circ}$,

There is also an oblique line passing through D and intersecting AC; the problem statement explains that this line is the perpendicular bisector of AC. Reasoning: Because AB=AC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB. It is known that ∠BAC=130°, so ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-130°)/2=25°. Because D is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, AD=CD. Thus in triangle ACD, AD=CD, so the base angles ∠CAD=∠ACD. Also because D is on BC, ∠ACD=∠ACB=25°, therefore ∠CAD=25°. So ∠BAD=∠BAC-∠CAD=130°-25°=105°.
